intro: Giving your opinion, asking for someone else's, and saying whether you agree or not.
p.me parece que.glosa: I think that, it seems to me that
p.me parece que.consejo: If your opinion is affirmative, the next verb is indicative: «me parece que es caro».
p.qué te parece.glosa: what do you think of it
p.qué te parece.consejo: To ask several people: «¿qué os parece?» in Spain or «¿qué les parece?» in Latin America.
p.creo que.consejo: Affirmative, indicative: «creo que es caro». Negative, subjunctive: «no creo que sea caro».
p.pienso que.consejo: Do not confuse it with «pienso» + infinitive, which expresses an intention: «pienso viajar».
p.en mi opinión.consejo: It usually goes first and is followed by a comma: «En mi opinión, es buena idea».
p.para mí.consejo: Here «mí» has an accent mark. Without it, «mi» is possessive: «mi casa».
p.estoy de acuerdo.consejo: It is said with «estar»: «estoy de acuerdo». Never «soy de acuerdo».
p.no estoy de acuerdo.consejo: To soften it: «no estoy del todo de acuerdo». It sounds kinder.
p.tienes razón.consejo: It is said with «tener»: «tienes razón». Never «eres razón» or «estás razón».
p.depende.consejo: With «de» it says what it depends on: «depende del precio». On its own it is a very common short answer.
p.por supuesto.consejo: You can also say «desde luego» or «claro». All three confirm strongly.
p.qué va.consejo: It is colloquial and emphatic: «¿Caro? ¡Qué va!». Avoid it in formal situations.
p.puede ser.consejo: It is a soft answer, neither yes nor no. «Quizá» and «a lo mejor» also work.
b1.texto:
To give your opinion use **creo que**, **pienso que**, **me parece que**, **para mí** or **en mi opinión**. If the opinion is affirmative, the verb is **indicative**: **Creo que es** caro. If you negate it, the verb is **subjunctive**: **No creo que sea** caro.

**Parecer** works like **gustar**: **me parece** caro, **me parecen** caros.

To ask for an opinion: **¿Qué te parece?** **¿Tú qué crees?**

To agree: **estoy de acuerdo**, **tienes razón**, **por supuesto**. To disagree: **no estoy de acuerdo**, **yo creo que no**, **¡qué va!**. And in between: **depende**, **puede ser**.

Watch the verbs: **estar** de acuerdo and **tener** razón.
b2.f0.texto: What do you think of the new flat?
b2.f1.texto: It seems a bit expensive to me.
b2.f2.texto: I think the neighbourhood is very good.
b2.f3.texto: The bedrooms seem small to me.
b2.f4.texto: In my opinion, the bedrooms are perfect.
b2.f5.texto: I don't think they are that big.
b2.f6.texto: Then let's go and see them again.
b4.texto:
After an affirmative opinion comes the **indicative**; after a negative one, the **subjunctive**:

- **Creo que** es buena idea.
- **No creo que** sea buena idea.
- **Me parece que** tienes razón.
- **No me parece que** tengas razón.

The verb **parecer** also links to an adjective and agrees with what is being judged: **me parece** caro, **me parecen** caros. The subjunctive of **ser** is **sea, seas, sea, seamos, seáis, sean**.
b4.e0.texto: I don't think it is a good idea.
b4.e2.texto: The prices seem very high to me.
b5.f0.texto: The kitchen table smells of coffee and orange sponge cake.
b5.f1.texto: On the checked tablecloth lie an old map and three colourful leaflets.
b5.f2.texto: Marta thinks the mountains are better for resting.
b5.f3.texto: Her brother Iván prefers the sea and dreams of a beach with white sand.
b5.f4.texto: Grandma listens in silence and stirs her coffee with a small spoon.
b5.f5.texto: Marta insists that the fresh air of the pines cures every kind of tiredness.
b5.f6.texto: Iván answers that the waves seem to him the best music in the world.
b5.f7.texto: The two siblings raise their voices and smile at the same time.
b5.f8.texto: Grandma leaves the spoon on the saucer and suggests a third idea.
b5.f9.texto: A small village between the sea and the mountains seems perfect to everyone.
b6.o0: Que lo que dices es correcto.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it: «tener razón» means to be right.
b6.o1: Que no está de acuerdo contigo.
b6.o1.refuerzo: On the contrary: «tienes razón» agrees with you.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That would be «depende». «Tienes razón» is a clear answer.
b6.pregunta: A friend says «Tienes razón». What does she think?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Ser» is not used here. With «de acuerdo» you use «estar».
b7.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «estoy de acuerdo». It is said with «estar».
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Tener» goes with «razón»: «tengo razón». Here you need «estar».
b7.pregunta: Which verb is used to show agreement?
b8.traduccion: What do you think of the new flat?
b9.o0: No creo que es buena idea.
b9.o0.refuerzo: After «no creo que» you use the subjunctive, not the indicative.
b9.o1: No creo que sea buena idea.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Well done! «No creo que» takes the subjunctive: «sea».
b9.o2: No creo que será buena idea.
b9.o2.refuerzo: The future does not work either: here you need the subjunctive.
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the verb agrees with «las habitaciones».
b11.o1.refuerzo: It is singular and «las habitaciones» is plural.
b11.o2.refuerzo: «Parezco» would be «I». Here the subject is the bedrooms.
b11.pregunta: There are several bedrooms. Which verb is missing?
b12.o0.refuerzo: No: «¡qué va!» is the opposite of showing agreement.
b12.o1.refuerzo: It is not about leaving: it is a fixed expression to deny.
b12.o2.refuerzo: That's it: it is a colloquial, emphatic denial.
b12.pregunta: Someone says «¡Qué va!». What does it mean?
p.habitaciones.consejo: It is the plural of «la habitación»; the accent mark disappears in the plural. The «h» is silent.
p.perfectas.consejo: It agrees with «habitaciones»: feminine plural. The «ct» keeps both sounds: «per-FEK-tas».
p.sean.consejo: It is the subjunctive of «ser» for «ellos»: «no creo que sean». The «e» and «a» are separate syllables.
p.verlas.consejo: It is «ver» + «las»: the pronoun joins the infinitive. «Las» refers to «habitaciones».
p.folletos.consejo: It is the plural of «el folleto». The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.mar.consejo: It is usually masculine: «el mar». Poets and sailors also say «la mar».
p.sueña.consejo: It comes from «soñar»: the «o» becomes «ue». It takes «con»: «soñar con una playa».
p.remueve.consejo: It comes from «remover»: the «o» becomes «ue» in «remuevo», «remueves», «remueve».
p.cucharilla.consejo: It comes from «cuchara» + «-illa» (small). The «ch» is like English «ch».
p.asegura.consejo: It comes from «asegurar», from «seguro». «Asegura que…» introduces what she is sure of.
p.pinos.consejo: It is the plural of «el pino». Do not confuse it with «el pie» (foot).
p.cura.consejo: It comes from «curar», a regular verb. The related noun is «la cura»: the cure.
p.cansancios.consejo: It is the plural of «el cansancio». The «c» before «i» sounds «th»; the «s» stays «s».
p.olas.consejo: It is the plural of «la ola». Do not confuse it with «hola»: same sound, no «h».
p.mundo.consejo: «Del mundo» is common after a superlative: «el mejor del mundo». «Todo el mundo» means everyone.
p.levantan.consejo: «Levantar la voz» means to speak louder. The «v» sounds like «b».
p.tercera.consejo: It is the feminine of «tercero». Before a masculine noun it is «tercer»: «el tercer día».
p.perfecto.consejo: It changes with gender: «perfecto», «perfecta». The «ct» keeps both sounds.
p.dices.consejo: It comes from «decir»: the «e» becomes «i» in «digo», «dices», «dice».
p.correcto.consejo: It changes with gender: «correcto», «correcta». The «rr» is strong.
